evidence: M-O s.v. rice paddy: Velenovský (1891), inter orȳzēta
terms.comment: A modern word, made on orȳza, rice (Hor. S. 2.3.155), as olīvētum is made on olīva; Morgan–Owens cites it from the botanist Velenovský, of the rice fields on the plain of Plovdiv. Terraced fields are orȳzēta too: say how they climb the hill (see the examples).

phrases.latin: Vidēsne orȳzēta? Tōta aquā operta sunt.
phrases.english: Do you see the rice fields? They’re all under water.

phrases.latin: Orȳzēta per clīvōs gradātim ascendunt, quasi scālae ingentēs.
phrases.english: The rice terraces climb the slopes step by step, like giant stairs.

phrases.latin: Nōlī in orȳzētum dēscendere: lutum altum est.
phrases.english: Don’t go down into the paddy: the mud is deep.

phrases.latin: In plānitiē Philippopolēnsī inter orȳzēta itinere aberrāvī.
phrases.english: On the plain of Philippopolis I lost my way among the rice paddies.

sources: Lewis & Short: oryza · Lewis & Short: olivetum
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. rice paddy.
